reviewer_diagnosis_quoted: the check grades what its fixture answers, and the fixture answers a method name rather than validating an envelope, so anything that lives below the method name - the CAS fields, the two statuses it never emits, the status session leg it never requests, the table's method column and the mirrors it never exercises - is unasserted.

changes_in_tests_runtime_cli_contract.strict_host: new probe mode that mirrors internal/domain/client_protocol.go's DecodeEnvelope and refuses with its own codes (UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL, MISSING_FIELD:command_id/project_id/session_id/expected_revision/writer_epoch, ATTACKER_CLAIMED_EPOCH, MODEL_CHANGE_WITHOUT_EPOCH, UNEXPECTED_PAYLOAD_KEYS). The write-method table is duplicated on purpose: a fixture that imported the product's table could not refuse a product change.
changes_in_tests_runtime_cli_contract.inprogress_host: new probe mode answering HTTP 202 with status IN_PROGRESS, the status the previous fixture never emitted
changes_in_tests_runtime_cli_contract.wire_method_ledger: every probe host now records the method names it actually received, and a row requires each claimed operation leg to appear there

measurement: go build rc 0; the check program ran twice, both PASS at 95 assertions with zero failures (was 91).

ordering_lesson_recorded: the strict and in-progress rows rewrite this phase's config file, and the interactive phase further down inherits it: the first two runs failed W0503-INTERACTIVE-SENDS-LIST-CREATE-SEND until the previous content was restored at the end of the block. A new phase that writes shared state must hand the next phase the state it found.

disclosed_false_start: two failures of my own are recorded here rather than edited out. (1) The first attempt to run the mutant was dispatched as a background shell command feeding python through stdin; it died with WinError 123 before executing and the chained commit never ran, yet the draft already claimed the kill - it is now backed by the foreground measurement above. (2) The follow-up commit 5137d7f8 carried a message describing this measured kill and two frozen files, but its patch step crashed on a string/dict key before writing them, so the commit landed with an unpatched record and the files missing. This commit is the correction: the message was ahead of the evidence, and the evidence is what was brought up to it.
